parent_amount.meaning: locked amount A of the parent veNFT before split
parent_amount.evidence: `multiSplit()` burns the parent veNFT and mints multiple child veNFTs with proportional amounts calculated by integer division. For a parent with amount `A` and weights `w[i]`, each child receives `floor(A * w[i] / Σw)`. This truncation yields Σ(child) ≤ A and usually Σ(child) < A when `A` is not exactly divisible by `Σw`. The parent is first burned and then children are minted, so the rounding remainder is lost on-chain.

parent_is_permanent.meaning: parent veNFT is a permanent lock (originalLocked.isPermanent == true)
parent_is_permanent.evidence: When the parent is a permanent lock (`originalLocked.isPermanent == true`), `multiSplit()` never adjusts the global `permanentLockBalance` to reflect the (smaller) sum of the new child amounts. As a result, `permanentLockBalance` remains at its pre-split value, while the true sum of permanent child locks is smaller due to rounding. This breaks the invariant that `permanentLockBalance` equals the sum of all permanently locked amounts and contaminates global voting-supply snapshots (via `_checkpoint`, which records `last_point.permanent = permanentLockBalance`).
